hints.title: Simulation Reproduction Obstacle
hints.text: Arbitrary push and pop orders may conflict with strict last-in first-out order. How can simulating the operations sequentially with an auxiliary buffer confirm whether the target sequence is reproducible?

hints.title: Greedy Pop Invariant
hints.text: Whenever the top of the buffer matches the current element expected by popped, it must be popped immediately because delaying would bury it under subsequent pushes.

hints.title: Sequential Push-Greedy-Pop Procedure
hints.text: Iterate through pushed, pushing each value onto an auxiliary list. While the list is non-empty and its top equals popped[j], pop from the list and advance pointer j. Return whether j equals the length of popped.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of pushed/popped arrays (1 <= N <= 1000)
complexity.notes: Each value is pushed and popped at most once.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Exploring all permutation sequences of pushes and pops runs in exponential Catalan number time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Greedy simulation avoids backtracking and operates in linear O(N) time and space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Understanding why the greedy choice of popping as early as possible is optimal and provably sufficient.
